pr_body:
Adds a new component to the _id in TSDS containing a hash of time_series_metric field names

fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/99123
pr_title: Don't reject docs as duplicates if they have different metrics
pr_comment: Hi @felixbarny, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

We discussed the following: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/120280#discussion_r1923925576 in another meeting and the behaviour mentioned is an unwanted side effect of this change. 

We talked about anther way to deal with accepting documents with the same tsid and timestamp but different metrics and that is via updates with upserts (meaning index if not exist and otherwise update). Since logically this is an update. However currently data streams don't allow any other operation type than create and we are unsure of the performance impact of bulk with updates operations(instead of create ops).

However tsdb data streams could support updates (and other operation types), because of the fact that tsdb data streams always route to the same backing index (using `@timestamp` field). Additionally with tsdb we already generate an _id based the document's content (dimension fields and `@timestamp`), so the optimizations we do for create ops with auto generated ids don't apply here, so perhaps change bulk api's operation type from create to update with upsert will not be too much.
I'm closing this as non-viable according to the reasoning in the comment above.

review_comment: Maybe make this similar to `TimeSeriesRoutingHashFieldType`? Overtime doc values and field data support was added to it.
Is that so that we can expose the `_ts_metric_names_hash` to users? As this is an internal field, I'm not sure we'd want to do that. What would be the benefits of that?
Curious to see the impact on disk usage because of this. I suspect most documents with a time series block will have the same set of metrics and therefor a same hash?

I think so, too. But probably we should also sort by _ts_metric_names_hash in addition to _tsid and @timestamp, to aid with compression in case there are docs with different metrics. This would presumably also make the metric doc values more dense, as it would ensure docs with the same set of populated metric fields are stored in proximity. WDYT?
I don't think it's worth adding this to the sort config, the values will be different hashes so we won't get much by sorting. Besides, the metrics will be different.

The sort config I was thinking about is `_tsid` (asc), `_ts_metric_names_hash` (asc), `@timestamp` (desc). The metric names hash would act as a kind-of tie breaker when the `_tsid` is the same. It would sort documents with the same set of metrics in proximity to one another. This should make their doc_values more dense. It would also make run-length-encoding for `_ts_metric_names_hash` more effective. Storage-wise, the effect would be similar to having a separate `_tsid` for documents with different metrics with the benefit that we can still properly detect counter rate resets as the `_tsid` doesn't actually change.
Would 4 bytes suffice here? I assume these conflicts are fairly infrequent in the first place.
I think that's probably fine, yes. The question is which hashing algorithm to use that produces a 32 bit value. Let's discuss that on your comment on `RoutingPathFields`.
These seem expensive.. how about using (XORing?) the `hashCode()` of each string?

This is what we're doing for the _tsid as well but with a re-used buffer, so that we don't need to allocate a separate buffer for each string in order to hash it. The benefit is that we can use a hash (murmurhash3) with a better distribution/fewer collisions compared to `hashCode`, the tradeoff is performance. But if we're not too concerned about collisions, we could also just use `TreeSet#hashCode`, or a variation that uses XOR'ing or multiplying each string's hash code by 31 (similar to how `String#hashCode` works).
